text:
alex: quick follow-up from the rfc — proposing a "soft gatekeeper" fallback layer for v4->v5 migration. idea is: accept v4 shapes, attach a lightweight transform passthrough, and route through a fallback circuit when downstream model/schema mismatch is detected. low-risk opt-in first.
maya: can you sketch the failure modes? i worry about silent corruption (wrong field mapped) vs obvious errors. :thinking_face:
sam: failure modes: 1) transform mismatch -> explicit 400 (preferred) 2) unknown fields -> preserved and logged 3) subtle semantic drift (hard) -> surface telemetry + score regression tag
liam: important: keep latency budget tight. any transform must be O(1) and async-traceable. we should avoid per-request heavyweight parsing. maybe use header sniff + fast path.
alex: agreed. plan: header X-RW-GK: soft-optin to enable transform. default off. short-circuit hot path when header absent. also add negotiation probe so clients can detect capability.
rachel: rollout ops? do we canary by tenant? by route? need escape hatch for bad transforms.
alex: tenant-level opt-in first, then route-level for a subset. escape hatch: admin flag to disable gatekeeper per-tenant + metric alert on transform-error-rate > 0.5% triggers rollback.
maya: telemetry: add metric tags: gatekeeper.enabled, transform.version, transform.errors, transform.latency_ms. also sample payloads to s3 (redacted) for quick debug.
liam: circuit breaker parameters suggestion: 
```
- window: 1m
- error_threshold: 0.5%
- cooldown: 5m
- fail_open_on_unparseable: false
```
sam: also add a synthetic regression test in CI: feed known prompts and check embeddings / generation delta within epsilon. if transform causes quality drop, auto-reject rollout.
alex: good call. owners: @maya for telemetry/schema, @liam for perf/circuit, @rachel for rollout playbook, @sam for CI checks. i'll draft the follow-up rfc with these ops/runbook bits.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: gatekeeper-transform v0.1 -> staging at 4176543250 :rocket:
rachel: staging watch window 30m, ping on any anomaly, will coordinate post-mortem template if needed. :thumbsup:
